entityDescription:
Caledonian Photonics Limited is a micro-SME in the field of robust, miniaturised solid-state lasers. The company has expertise in design for manufacture, reliability and environmental insensitivity, with experience of the academic, scientific and defence markets. 

For the last 2 years, Caledonian Photonics has been involved in the development of narrow-linewidth lasers targeting the Quantum Technologies (QT) market. These developments have led to Caledonian Photonics' involvement in 3 Innovate-UK funded projects to further develop this technology and allow QT applications such as cold-atom gravimetry, inertial navigation and timing to leave the laboratory and operate robustly in the real-world.

In 2018 Caledonian Photonics won a DASA contract titled “Low Size, Weight, Power and Cost Monolithic Lasers For Man-Portable Applications”. This contract enabled Caledonian Photonics to demonstrate the production of novel monolithic optical assemblies and their use within laser resonators. Caledonian were subsequently awarded a follow-on contract to apply this technology to OPO systems. 
Dr Stephen Lee, founder and CEO, has 23 years of experience in solid-state lasers and their integration into optical systems. He developed this during his 6 years at Coherent as a senior laser design engineer engaged in new product design and introduction of broadly tunable Ti:Sapphire lasers for bioscience applications. Stephen then spent 10 years at Thales UK in the Defence Lasers product line where he acted as design authority for the defence lasers product line.

entityDescription: RU.DE – Associação de Desenvolvimento Rural / Rural Development Agency) is a private non-profit entity, established on 19th December 1991. It aims to promote the sustainable development of rural areas, as a way of attracting people and new activities, retaining populations and diversifying the social, economic and cultural basis of the Cova da Beira subregion. Its intervention territory is the subregion called Cova da Beira and includes the municipalities of Belmonte, Covilhã and Fundão. This sub-region has a total area of 1.373km2 and a current resident population of 87,471 inhabitants. RU.DE has been implementing the LEADER Programme since 1992. During this period, RU.DE has supported, with the LEADER Programme, more than 400 projects which represented an investment of more than 30 million euros in the territory. In the present programming period (2014-2020), RU.DE is the manager partner of the Local Action Group (LAG) Cova da Beira 2020. The LAG COVA DA BEIRA 2020 partnership involves 111 organizations representing different areas between the public, private and civil sectors. RUDE's intervention is based on logics of proximity and territorial cohesion, experimentation and innovation and, above all, on participatory methodologies with the involvement of local actors, creating responses to social, environmental and economic challenges. RU.DE is a recognized player in the strategic social and economic definition for the region and generates dynamics in its intervention territory through the generation and monitoring of innovative initiatives, especially on rural development, thus contributing to competitiveness, sustainability of the territories and quality of life for populations.

TravelAi is a European Space Agency BIC programme Alumni that relies on the use of Galileo and GPS technologies. With a multi-country team based in the UK (HQ), Portugal and Finland, the all engineering team has built a Technology Stack to help understand how citizens around the world use transport systems. Be that by public or private transit, human powered or motorised and without the limitations of geographic borders or even requiring CAPEX heavy physical or sensor infrastructure because we leverage the ubiquity of smartphones.

This automatic software development kit (SDK) can be embedded into existing Android and iOS apps to allow our B2B clients to identify the route, mode of transport and time that their customers travel so that they can better meet their needs and optimise their services for them. Including travel by car, bus, bike, train, tram, metro, plane and by foot. This technology is used by transport service providers such as train and bus operators, municipalities and their transit authorities, and infrastructure owners all wanting to solve mobility related challenges. 
We have also identified use cases for the same SDK that uses our automatic multi-modal detection solution to automatically carbon footprint an individuals mobility habits by applying the relevant carbon factor to the distance travelled by by the user. 

There are also applications to identify how transport systems improve social mobility by helping to capture end-to-end origin-destination matrices style journey histories. Even encouraging more active travel by virtue of our ability to capture both human powered travels and motorised.

COVID19 has revealed another application for our IP stack. Contact or spread tracing is a critical tool health professionals use to identify how transmitters of a pathogen infect others. Helping to isolate those who pose a risk while simultaneously providing data for epidemiologists to profile a pathogens characteristics. Providing the opportunity to equip medical professionals, governments and citizens with a tool to fight this global pandemic.

entityDescription:
The Department of Biology at the University of Florence has a long history that has its roots well before the founding of the University itself. It is in fact the heir to the naturalistic studies that brought prestige to the city of Florence and contributed to the development of natural sciences worldwide. Indeed, it is from the mid-18th century that the Museum of Physics and Natural History was founded, located even then in Via Romana in one of the Department's current locations. Still, the Department of Biology houses in the building on Via La Pira the Italian Botanical Society, founded in Florence in 1888, which traces its origin to the first botanical society in Europe (the Florentine Botanical Society) founded in Florence in 1716.
On this distinguished past the Department of Biology has not rested, and in recent decades, through continuous renewal, it has now moved to the forefront in many important areas of biology. The disciplines in which the research conducted by the Department of Biology is currently an international excellence are numerous: microbiology, genetics, physiology, botany in all its aspects, zoology with a particular contribution from ethology, ecology of both marine and terrestrial environments, anthropology, cytology and histology, comparative anatomy, and, as a common thread, the history of biology and natural sciences with evolutionary studies.
The solid scientific basis on which the Department of Biology is founded is its interest in experimental research, and within this framework it should be emphasized that the scientific work conducted by researchers and technicians in the Department is strongly oriented toward basic research, but carefully and increasingly considers its applications, responding to current needs for innovation and development. Building on robust basic knowledge, researchers in the Department of Biology recognize that good research always has within it the preconditions for possible applications and are therefore interested in offering their knowledge and technologies to develop potential applications.

Building on the strong interest in basic scientific research and its applications, the Department's teaching and technical staff is able to handle a good deal of teaching in basic and applied biological and natural sciences disciplines of different educational tracks: biology, natural sciences, biotechnology, at the level of bachelor's, master's and doctoral degree programs. Teaching in experimental disciplines such as biology finds its natural complement in intensive laboratory and field exercises that provide students with a practical foundation for their future profession.

Facilities
The rich and multifaceted history of the Department of Biology still surfaces in the facilities in which its various components are housed and interact effectively with each other. On the one hand, the historic buildings in the center of Florence, in Via La Pira, Via del Proconsolo and Via Romana, which are also home to the Museum of Natural History, represent the link with the more properly naturalistic disciplines while the premises at the Scientific Pole in Sesto Fiorentino particularly accommodate the physiological and molecular disciplines.

entityDescription: ThePlanning and Scheduling Technology(PST) Lab has been founded in 1997 as a research group focused on automated and interactive techniques for planning problems. We have obtained results on specialized constraint reasoning, (meta) heuristics for scheduling, mixed-initiative problem solving, timeline-based planning. The group has been involved for over ten years in a collaboration with the European Space Agency (ESA). Three of our problem solving tools are in continuous daily use in the mission planning ground facility at ESA-ESOC, Darmstadt. During the last five years we have broadened our research interests toward new areas thus acquiring competences in robotics, ambient assisted living, cognitive systems for training, and health systems for ageing well. In FP7 we have projects in different topics (Space, ICT, Security, and AAL).
